public_rationale: Both parts hold for the period described. On mimicry: in a controlled March 2025 Turing test, GPT-4.5 was judged human 73% of the time, more often than real people. On gaps: when ARC-AGI-2 launched a week before the post, frontier models scored about 1-4% while human panels averaged 60%. A late-2024 planning study found even OpenAI's o1 far from solving PlanBench. One counterpoint is that o3 matched humans on ARC-AGI-1 in December 2024, so the gaps were narrowing on some tests. Still, the claim that a lot was missing in reasoning and planning fits the evidence from the time.
limitations: Common sense was not measured directly in the cited items.
'A lot' is vague; reasonable readers could weigh the fast gains differently.
Turing-test and PlanBench sources are preprints.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: two parts. (1) AI got much better at imitating human conversation between 2014 and early 2025. (2) Systems at the post date still fell well short of humans on tests of reasoning, planning and common sense.
Target period runs from 2014 to the post date.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence of strong human-mimicry gains, such as passing a controlled Turing test, plus evaluations from around early 2025 showing large gaps versus humans on reasoning, planning or common-sense tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that mimicry did not improve much, or that systems around April 2025 matched humans broadly on reasoning, planning and common-sense evaluations.

evidence.excerpt: When prompted to adopt a humanlike persona, GPT-4.5 was judged to be the human 73% of the time: significantly more often than interrogators selected the real human participant.
evidence.explanation: A pre-registered three-party Turing test found GPT-4.5 judged human more often than real humans. That shows great progress in human mimicry.

evidence.excerpt: The Arc Prize Foundation had over 400 people take ARC-AGI-2 to establish a human baseline. On average, “panels” of these people got 60% of the test’s questions right — much better than any of the models’ scores.
evidence.explanation: At launch, a week before the post, frontier models scored about 1-4% on a novel reasoning test where human panels got 60%. That is a large reasoning gap.

evidence.excerpt: As we shall see, while o1's performance is a quantum improvement on the benchmark, outpacing the competition, it is still far from saturating it.
evidence.explanation: The best reasoning model of late 2024 was still far from solving a standard planning benchmark. That fits the claim's planning gap, though the paper also notes big gains.

evidence.excerpt: ARC-AGI-1 was unbeaten for roughly five years until December 2024, when OpenAI released its advanced reasoning model, o3, which outperformed all other AI models and matched human performance on the evaluation.
evidence.explanation: Some reasoning tests had been matched at human level by late 2024. That cuts against the claim's degree, though not against its core.
